newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday May 16.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* In an interview, prime minister Romano Prodi, said Italy still had to face some sacrifices but economic recovery was approaching. After his first year in office, Prodi admitted his hard left ally, the Communist Refoundation, did slow the government's reforming process but he said that it was better to proceed little by little and be backed by all his political allies (Corriere della Sera).

* Finance minister Vincenzo Visco said the new instrument to evalute income and standard of living for tax contributors would be ready in a couple of months. Visco also said Italy's three year programme of economic targets (DPEF) would probably be ready by the end of next week (all).
* A report by national statistics institute ISTAT showed Italian industrial output fell by a provisional 3.6 percent year-on-year in March compared with a fall of 3.1 percent in February (all).

* Giorgio Fossa, the president of Italian industrialists' association Confindustria, said he was not as confident as Prodi that the country's economy would recover. Fossa called for structural measures also in order to favour a cut in interest rates (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
